Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36582: test: reorder functional tests by current runtimes

649e075655c653f0581ba7a28f7bda2b347fad80 test: move slow tests to run earlier (ViniciusCestarii)
6a59afd317d31e844631ec8b031feb94399e1196 test: move fast tests to run later (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  After #36439, #36440 and #36446 some tests got much faster.

  Move tests that finish faster to run later and move tests that are slow to run earlier.

  Timings from master CI run [39389906008](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/39389906008):

  | Test | Bucket (before → after) | CI median | CI max |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `interface_http.py` | <30s (late) → <60s (first) | 53s | 60s (TSan) |
  | `feature_maxuploadtarget.py` | <2m → <30s (first) | 10s | 44s (Windows native, VS) |
  | `feature_torcontrol.py` | <30s (late) → <30s (early) | 17s | 20s (macOS native) |
  | `wallet_conflicts.py` | <5m → <30s | 4s | 11s (TSan) |
  | `p2p_node_network_limited.py --v1transport` | <5m → <30s | 6s | 18s (TSan) |
  | `p2p_node_network_limited.py --v2transport` | <5m → <30s | 6s | 17s (TSan) |
  | `wallet_backup.py` | <60s → <30s | 8s | 17s (TSan) |
  | `wallet_address_types.py` | <60s → <30s | 7s | 20s (TSan) |
  | `p2p_sendheaders.py` | <60s → <30s | 3s | 8s (TSan) |
  | `feature_maxtipage.py` | <60s → <30s | 5s | 11s (TSan) |
  | `feature_csv_activation.py` | <60s → <30s | 6s | 13s (TSan) |
  | `feature_segwit.py --v1transport` | <60s → <30s | 4s | 12s (TSan) |
  | `feature_segwit.py --v2transport` | <60s → <30s | 4s | 14s (TSan) |

  Locally (`test_runner.py -j=18 --randomseed=1`) with these changes I got: 84s -> 78s (median of 3 runs)

Pull request description:

  This is a low-prio style cleanup for years, but:

  * It is tedious and possibly distracting to do it manually when touching the line for other reasons.
  * The topic recently came up again when discussing log injection (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35833#issuecomment-5113804332)

  So I wonder if a simple scripted-diff can cover the bulk of the changes now, with hopefully little conflicts with reviewed pull requests.

  (Removing the trailing newlines from the remaining log messages is trivial and can be done in a later pull)

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36573: test: cover gettxspendingprevout error without txospenderindex

edf0d13ad5ff9035ad7a0ff7bc38610edb952b2d test: cover gettxspendingprevout error without txospenderindex (mercie-ux)

Pull request description:

  Add functional coverage for the `gettxspendingprevout` error raised when `mempool_only=false`, no matching spend is in the mempool, and `txospenderindex` is unavailable.

  The combined unit and functional coverage report shows this throw in `src/rpc/mempool.cpp` is never reached:
  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/71fa0439278f1d11c9a1aabe67312dcdf1cc8757/src/rpc/mempool.cpp#L1080

  The existing test already queries node2 without the index, but `mempool_only` defaults to `true` in that case, so the error is only reachable when `mempool_only=false` is passed explicitly.

  The test now checks both sides on node2 with `mempool_only=false`: it  succeeds while the spends are still in the mempool, and raises the error once they are mined.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36177: net: fix startup failures from stale Tor examples

6c7c27f615a5b74e0aa921b8f103bf468a510aac doc: use onion in proxy help and examples (Lőrinc)
fd65406b39a844d2093c33e7662f79be2857d197 net: preserve network name case in proxy errors (Lőrinc)
b0375749d4d4763efa95be2f0b0bcbe20e7d9a78 refactor: share proxy network parsing (Lőrinc)
332c3e8e3e176b6d7e83960325ca3d8d1859d7eb test: characterize proxy network name errors (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** #34031 removed `tor` as a network name, but the `-proxy` help and Tor documentation still advertise it, and following those examples fails at startup.
  The proxy option also maintains its own network-name mapping while `-onlynet` and `getnodeaddresses` use the shared parser.

  **Fix:** Reuse the shared parser and canonical network names for `-proxy`, and document `onion` consistently. Unsupported network names are now echoed as supplied, matching the other interfaces, while accepted names remain case-insensitive.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36559: test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex

2f7622e3f6f7ef431a7d5ec522958da62f33cec4 test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex (Kevin Ravensberg)

Pull request description:

  `feature_anchors.py` builds the expected `anchors.dat` substring from each peer's port with `hex(port)[2:]`, which is not zero-padded. The port is serialized as two bytes, so for ports below 4096 the expected string is one hex digit short and `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` fails.

  This only shows up with a non-default port range, for example when avoiding local listeners:

  ```
  TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100 test/functional/feature_anchors.py
  ```

  fails on master with `AssertionError` at the `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` line and passes with this change; the default range still passes.

  ---
  Disclosure: AI (Claude Fable 5.1) was used to find this issue and to draft this PR.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36407: test: make orphanage_dos_many fill the orphanage

86ff13a0af0679ee0c725bac9c64c3e373cb0283 test: make orphanage_dos_many fill the orphanage (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  `test_orphanage_dos_many` checks that a normal peer's orphan survives while DoS peers flood the orphanage. I found that the orphanage never fills: the 60 peers send the same 51 orphans as `tx`, and a `tx` already held as an orphan is dropped in `ReceivedTx` without recording its sender. The orphanage peaks at 152 announcements against a limit of 3000, so nothing is evicted.

  Here the first peer sends the orphans and the other 59 announce them by `inv`, which does add them as announcers. The test now asserts that the orphanage holds 3000 announcements, instead of asserting on what it sends. It takes about as long as before.

  If `LimitOrphans` is changed to evict the normal peer's orphan first, the test used to pass and now fails. (`test_orphanage_dos_large` already catches that change.)

  Found while porting these tests to https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-node-tests.

  *Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36341: wallet: return error from bitcoin-wallet create

f64d33672fe1488b49254a634cbecfd9ce4ca179 wallet: return error from bitcoin-wallet create (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `bitcoin-wallet create` exits with status 0 even when the wallet couldn't be created:

  ```
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create   # first time, ok
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create
  Failed to create database path '.../regtest/wallets/w1'. Database already exists.
  $ echo $?
  0
  ```

  In `ExecuteWalletToolFunc` the `create` branch only does something when `MakeWallet` succeeds and then falls through to `return true`. The other commands (`info`, `dump`, `createfromdump`) all return false on failure. So scripts that check the exit code think the wallet was created.

  This returns false when `MakeWallet` fails, the same way `info` does. The added check in `tool_wallet.py` runs `create` on the existing wallet `foo` and expects exit code 1. It fails on master (`not(0 == 1)`) and passes with the fix.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36339: wallet: avoid int overflow in listtransactions

9cff82fd5b15bc2aa2c7778b61212876433a8219 wallet: avoid int overflow in listtransactions (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `listtransactions` adds `count` and `skip` as `int`. Each one is checked to be non-negative, but their sum can still go past INT_MAX:

  ```
  bitcoin-cli -regtest listtransactions "*" 2147483647 1
  ```

  On master this crashes the node. The overflowed sum is negative, so the loop stops after the first entry. The clamp after the loop overflows the same way and doesn't fix `nCount`, so `push_backV` gets an iterator range about 2^31 elements before `rend()`. UBSan reports `signed integer overflow: 1 + 2147483647` at transactions.cpp:584, and ASan then reports a BUS error in `UniValue::push_backV`.

  This parses `count` and `skip` as `uint32_t` through `self.Arg` (which also handles the defaults and rejects negative values, so the manual checks go away) and adds them up in 64 bits, where the sum can't overflow. The functional test calls `listtransactions` with count + skip above INT_MAX and up to UINT32_MAX and checks the results match a normal-sized request. It times out on master (the node crashes) and passes with the fix. I also ran it on an ASan/UBSan build.

  `listrawtransactions` counts differently and isn't affected.

commit.message:
test: cover gettxspendingprevout error without txospenderindex

When `mempool_only=false` is passed to a node without `txospenderindex`
and the mempool has no spend for a requested outpoint, the RPC throws
"Mempool lacks a relevant spend, and txospenderindex is unavailable."
This path was not covered by any test.

The existing node2 query does not reach it because `mempool_only`
defaults to `true` when the index is unavailable. Pass it explicitly
and check both cases: the call succeeds while the spends are still in
the mempool, and raises the error once they are mined.

commit.message:
scripted-diff: [wallet] Remove trailing newlines from one-line log messages

The replacement skips log messages that contain: " or \
This keeps the script simple and allows to handle the special cases
manually.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-

 sed --in-place --regexp-extended 's/(WalletLogPrintf\([^\"]*"[^\"\\]*)\\n"([,)])/\1"\2/g' $(
       git grep -l --extended-regexp 'WalletLogPrintf' ./src
 )

-END VERIFY SCRIPT-
